articles.title: 完型 · 高智力是否存在进化代价
articles.context: 动物智力、进化成本与反向观察人类。文章从果蝇实验切入，讨论智力的能量与学习成本，再设想动物研究人类会问什么。语气理性、略带幽默，在反直觉结论和结尾问题处加强重音。
rows: Research on animal intelligence always makes us wonder just how smart humans are.
关于动物智力的研究总会让我们反过来思考：人类究竟有多聪明。
Consider the fruit-fly experiments described by Carl Zimmer in the Science Times.
想想卡尔·齐默在《科学时报》中介绍的果蝇实验。
Fruit flies who were taught to be smarter than the average fruit fly tended to live shorter lives.
那些被训练得比普通果蝇更聪明的果蝇，往往活得更短。
This suggests that dimmer bulbs burn longer, that there is an advantage in not being too bright.
这似乎表明：灯泡越暗反而烧得越久，也就是说，不那么聪明可能具有某种优势。
Intelligence, it turns out, is a high-priced option.
事实证明，智力是一种代价高昂的选择。
It takes more upkeep, burns more fuel and is slow off the starting line because it depends on learning—a gradual process—instead of instinct.
智力需要更多维护、消耗更多能量，而且起步较慢，因为它依赖的是学习——一个渐进的过程——而不是本能。
Plenty of other species are able to learn, and one of the things they've apparently learned is when to stop.
许多其他物种也能够学习，而它们显然学会的事情之一，就是知道什么时候该停止继续学习。
Is there an adaptive value to limited intelligence?
有限的智力是否具有适应价值？
That's the question behind this new research.
这正是这项新研究背后的问题。
Instead of casting a wistful glance backward at all the species we've left in the dust IQ-wise, it implicitly asks what the real costs of our own intelligence might be.
这项研究不再带着自得回望那些在智力上被我们远远甩在身后的物种，而是含蓄地追问：人类自身的智力究竟付出了什么真实代价。
This is on the mind of every animal we've ever met.
这大概也是我们遇到过的每一种动物都想知道的问题。
Research on animal intelligence also makes us wonder what experiments animals would perform on humans if they had the chance.
动物智力研究还会让我们设想：如果动物有机会，它们会在人类身上做什么实验。
Every cat with an owner, for instance, is running a small-scale study in operant conditioning.
比如，每一只有主人的猫，其实都像是在进行一项小规模的操作性条件反射研究。
We believe that if animals ran the labs, they would test us to determine the limits of our patience, our faithfulness, our memory for locations.
我们相信，如果实验室由动物掌管，它们会测试我们，以确定人类在耐心、忠诚以及地点记忆方面的极限。
They would try to decide what intelligence in humans is really for, not merely how much of it there is.
它们会试图判断，人类智力究竟是用来做什么的，而不只是测量我们拥有多少智力。
Above all, they would hope to study a fundamental question: Are humans actually aware of the world they live in?
最重要的是，它们会希望研究一个根本问题：人类是否真的意识到自己生活在怎样的世界里？
So far the results are inconclusive.
到目前为止，结果仍然没有定论。

articles.title: 阅读一 · 用新习惯打开创新思维
articles.context: 习惯、创造力与创新主题。文章先打破“习惯与创新相悖”的直觉，再从脑科学和思维模式说明有意识培养新习惯能够开辟新的思考路径。
rows: 习惯是一件很有意思的事情。
We reach for them mindlessly, setting our brains on auto-pilot and relaxing into the unconscious comfort of familiar routine.
我们常常不假思索地依赖习惯，让大脑进入“自动驾驶”状态，安然沉入熟悉日常所带来的无意识舒适感中。
"Not choice, but habit rules the unreflecting herd," William Wordsworth said in the 19th century.
19世纪，威廉·华兹华斯曾说：“支配不加反思的人群的不是选择，而是习惯。”
In the ever-changing 21st century, even the word “habit” carries a negative implication.
在不断变化的21世纪，甚至“习惯”这个词本身也带有负面意味。
So it seems paradoxical to talk about habits in the same context as creativity and innovation.
因此，把习惯与创造力和创新放在同一语境中谈论，似乎有些自相矛盾。

But brain researchers have discovered that when we consciously develop new habits, we create parallel paths, and even entirely new brain cells, that can jump our trains of thought onto new, innovative tracks.
但脑科学研究者发现，当我们有意识地培养新习惯时，会形成平行路径，甚至生成全新的脑细胞，从而让思维列车跃迁到新的、富有创新性的轨道上。
Rather than dismissing ourselves as unchangeable creatures of habit, we can instead direct our own change by consciously developing new habits.
与其认定自己是无法改变的习惯动物，不如通过有意识地培养新习惯，主动引导自身改变。
In fact, the more new things we try — the more we step outside our comfort zone — the more inherently creative we become, both in the workplace and in our personal lives.
事实上，我们尝试的新事物越多，越经常走出舒适区，无论在工作还是个人生活中，我们就越会自然而然地变得更有创造力。
But don't bother trying to kill off old habits; once those ruts of procedure are worn into the brain, they're there to stay.
但别费力试图消灭旧习惯；一旦那些固定程序在大脑里磨出了车辙，它们就会长久存在。
Instead, the new habits we deliberately press into ourselves create parallel pathways that can bypass those old roads.
相反，我们有意识压入自身的新习惯会形成平行路径，从而绕开那些旧道路。
“The first thing needed for innovation is a fascination with wonder,” says Dawna Markova, author of The Open Mind.
“创新首先需要的是对惊奇保持着迷。”《开放的心智》作者多娜·马尔科娃说。
“But we are taught instead to ‘decide,’ just as our president calls himself ‘the Decider.’”
“但我们接受的教育却是要去‘做决定’，就像我们的总统把自己称作‘决断者’一样。”
She adds, however, that “to decide is to kill off all possibilities but one.
不过她补充说：“做决定，就意味着除了一种可能性之外，把其他所有可能性都排除掉。
A good innovational thinker is always exploring the many other possibilities.”
优秀的创新思考者总是在探索许多其他的可能性。”
All of us work through problems in ways of which we're unaware, she says.
她说，我们每个人解决问题时都会采用一些自己并未意识到的方式。

Researchers in the late 1960s discovered that humans are born with the capacity to approach challenges in four primary ways: analytically, procedurally, relationally (or collaboratively) and innovatively.
20世纪60年代末的研究者发现，人天生具有以四种基本方式应对挑战的能力：分析式、程序式、关系式（或协作式）和创新式。
At the end of adolescence, however, the brain shuts down half of that capacity, preserving only those modes of thought that have seemed most valuable during the first decade or so of life.
然而到了青春期末期，大脑会关闭其中一半能力，只保留那些在人生最初十来年中显得最有价值的思维模式。
The current emphasis on standardized testing highlights analysis and procedure, meaning that few of us inherently use our innovative and collaborative modes of thought.
当前对标准化考试的强调突出的是分析和程序，这意味着我们当中很少有人会本能地运用创新式和协作式思维。
“This breaks the major rule in the American belief system— that anyone can do anything,” explains M. J. Ryan, author of the 2006 book This Year I Will... and Ms. Markova's business partner.
“这打破了美国信念体系中的一条重要原则——任何人都可以做任何事。”2006年《今年我将……》一书作者、马尔科娃的商业伙伴M. J. Ryan解释道。
“That’s a lie that we have perpetuated, and it fosters commonness.
“这是我们一直延续的一个谎言，它培养的是平庸。
Knowing what you're good at and doing even more of it creates excellence.”
知道自己擅长什么，并把它做得更多、更好，才会创造卓越。”
This is where developing new habits comes in.
这正是培养新习惯发挥作用的地方。

articles.title: 阅读二 · 商业 DNA 检测的流行与局限
articles.context: 消费级 DNA 检测与科学可靠性。文章先介绍亲子鉴定套件和祖源检测的流行，再从谱系范围、数据库质量与算法透明度三个方面质疑其精确性。语气理性、审慎，在“false precision”和数据库局限处加强重音。
rows: It is a wise father that knows his own child, but today a man can boost his paternal wisdom—or at least confirm that he's the kid's dad.
俗话说，真正聪明的父亲才了解自己的孩子；但如今，一个男人可以借助技术提升这种“父亲的智慧”——至少可以确认自己是不是孩子的生父。
All he needs to do is shell out $30 for a paternity testing kit (PTK) at his local drugstore—and another $120 to get the results.
他只需在当地药店花30美元买一套亲子鉴定试剂盒，再支付120美元就能拿到检测结果。

More than 60,000 people have purchased the PTKs since they first became available without prescriptions last year, according to Doug Fogg, chief operating officer of Identigene, which makes the over-the-counter kits.
生产这种非处方试剂盒的 Identigene 公司首席运营官道格·福格称，自去年这类产品首次无需处方便可购买以来，已有超过6万人购买。
More than two dozen companies sell DNA tests directly to the public, ranging in price from a few hundred dollars to more than $2,500.
已有二十多家公司直接面向公众销售 DNA 检测服务，价格从几百美元到2500多美元不等。
Among the most popular are paternity and kinship testing, which adopted children can use to find their biological relatives and families can use to track down kids put up for adoption.
最受欢迎的服务之一是亲子和亲缘关系检测：被收养的孩子可以借此寻找血缘亲属，家庭也可以寻找曾被送养的孩子。
DNA testing is also the latest rage among passionate genealogists—and supports businesses that offer to search for a family's geographic roots.
DNA 检测还成了热衷家谱研究者的新潮流，也催生了帮助人们追寻家族地理起源的商业服务。
Most tests require collecting cells by swabbing saliva in the mouth and sending it to the company for testing.
大多数检测都要求用拭子从口腔唾液中采集细胞，再寄给公司进行检测。
All tests require a potential candidate with whom to compare DNA.
所有这类检测都需要一个潜在对象，以便进行 DNA 比对。
但一些观察者对此持怀疑态度。
‘There's a kind of false precision being hawked by people claiming they are doing ancestry testing,’ says Troy Duster, a New York University sociologist.
纽约大学社会学家特洛伊·达斯特说：“一些声称从事祖源检测的人正在兜售一种虚假的精确性。”
He notes that each individual has many ancestors—numbering in the hundreds just a few centuries back.
他指出，每个人都有许多祖先；仅仅向前追溯几个世纪，祖先数量就会达到数百人。
Yet most ancestry testing only considers a single lineage, either the Y chromosome inherited through men in a father's line or mitochondrial DNA, which is passed down only from mothers.
然而，大多数祖源检测只考察一条血缘线：要么分析父系男性传递的 Y 染色体，要么分析只由母亲传下来的线粒体 DNA。

This DNA can reveal genetic information about only one or two ancestors, even though, for example, just three generations back people also have six other great-grandparents or, four generations back, 14 other great-great-grandparents.
这种 DNA 只能揭示一两个祖先的遗传信息；但举例来说，仅向前追溯三代，一个人还会有另外六位曾祖父母，追溯四代则还会有另外14位高祖父母。
Critics also argue that commercial genetic testing is only as good as the reference collections to which a sample is compared.
批评者还指出，商业基因检测的可靠程度取决于用于比对的参考数据库质量。
Databases used by some companies don't rely on data collected systematically but rather lump together information from different research projects.
一些公司使用的数据库并不是建立在系统采集的数据之上，而只是把不同研究项目的信息拼在一起。
don't rely on data collected systematically
This means that a DNA database may have a lot of data from some regions and not others, so a person's test results may differ depending on the company that processes the results.
这意味着 DNA 数据库可能在某些地区数据很多、在另一些地区却很少，因此同一个人的检测结果可能会因处理检测的公司不同而有所差异。
In addition, the computer programs a company uses to estimate relationships may be patented and not subject to peer review or outside evaluation.
此外，公司用于推断亲缘关系的计算机程序可能受到专利保护，因此不接受同行评议或外部评价。

articles.title: 阅读三 · 教育、生产率与贫困国家的经济发展
articles.context: 教育与经济增长的因果关系。文章反驳‘先大规模教育才能增长’的常规看法，用美国工厂与墨西哥工人案例说明在职训练可快速提高生产率，再论证生产率增长反过来推动教育发展。语气分析性强，反常识论点和因果链处加强重音。
rows: The relationship between formal education and economic growth in poor countries is widely misunderstood by economists and politicians alike.
贫困国家中正规教育与经济增长之间的关系，普遍被经济学家和政治家误解。

Progress in both areas is undoubtedly necessary for the social, political, and intellectual development of these and all other societies; however, the conventional view that education should be one of the very highest priorities for promoting rapid economic development in poor countries is wrong.
这两个领域的进步无疑都是这些国家乃至所有社会实现社会、政治和智力发展的必要条件；然而，把教育视为贫困国家推动快速经济发展的最高优先事项之一，这种传统看法是错误的。
We are fortunate that it is, because building new educational systems there and putting enough people through them to improve economic performance would require two or three generations.
幸好这种看法是错的，因为如果要靠建立新的教育体系，并让足够多的人接受这种教育来改善经济表现，往往需要两三代人的时间。

The findings of a research institution have consistently shown that workers in all countries can be trained on the job to achieve radically higher productivity and, as a result, radically higher standards of living.
一家研究机构的发现一贯表明，各国工人都可以通过在职培训显著提高生产率，并由此大幅提高生活水平。
Ironically, the first evidence for this idea appeared in the United States.
颇具讽刺意味的是，这一观点的第一批证据恰恰出现在美国。

Not long ago, with the country entering a recession and Japan at its pre-bubble peak, the U.S. workforce was derided as poorly educated and one of the primary causes of the poor U.S. economic performance.
不久前，在美国陷入衰退、而日本处于泡沫破裂前的高峰时期，美国劳动力曾因教育水平低而遭到嘲讽，并被视为美国经济表现不佳的主要原因之一。
Japan was, and remains, the global leader in automotive-assembly productivity.
日本当时是、现在仍是汽车装配生产率的全球领先者。

Yet the research revealed that the U.S. factories of Honda, Nissan, and Toyota achieved about 95 percent of the productivity of their Japanese counterparts—a result of the training that U.S. workers received on the job.
然而研究发现，本田、日产和丰田在美国的工厂，其生产率达到了日本同类工厂的大约95%，而这正是在职培训美国工人的结果。

More recently, while examining housing construction, the researchers discovered that illiterate, non-English-speaking Mexican workers in Houston, Texas, consistently met best-practice labor productivity standards despite the complexity of the building industry's work.
更近的研究中，研究者考察住宅建设时发现，得克萨斯州休斯敦那些不识字、不会说英语的墨西哥工人，尽管建筑业工作十分复杂，却仍能持续达到最佳实践的劳动生产率标准。
What is the real relationship between education and economic development?
那么，教育与经济发展之间真正的关系究竟是什么？
We have to suspect that continuing economic growth promotes the development of education even when governments don't force it.
我们不得不怀疑，即使政府不强制推动，持续的经济增长本身也会促进教育发展。
even when governments don't force it
After all, that's how education got started.
毕竟，教育最初就是这样发展起来的。
When our ancestors were hunters and gatherers 10,000 years ago, they didn't have time to wonder much about anything besides finding food.
一万年前，当我们的祖先还是狩猎采集者时，他们几乎没有时间去思考寻找食物之外的事情。
Only when humanity began to get its food in a more productive way was there time for other things.
只有当人类开始以更高效的方式获取食物之后，才有时间从事其他活动。
As education improved, humanity's productivity potential increased as well.
随着教育改善，人类潜在的生产率也随之提高。
When the competitive environment pushed our ancestors to achieve that potential, they could in turn afford more education.
当竞争环境迫使我们的祖先把这种潜力转化为现实后，他们反过来便有能力承担更多教育。
This increasingly high level of education is probably a necessary, but not a sufficient, condition for the complex political systems required by advanced economic performance.
这种不断提高的教育水平，很可能是支撑高级经济表现所需复杂政治制度的必要条件，但并不是充分条件。
Thus poor countries might not be able to escape their poverty traps without political changes that may be possible only with broader formal education.
因此，如果没有政治变革，贫困国家可能无法摆脱贫困陷阱；而这种政治变革又可能只有在更广泛的正规教育基础上才有可能实现。
A lack of formal education, however, doesn't constrain the ability of the developing world's workforce to substantially improve productivity for the foreseeable future.
然而，在可预见的未来，正规教育不足并不会限制发展中国家劳动力大幅提高生产率的能力。
On the contrary, constraints on improving productivity explain why education isn't developing more quickly there than it is.
恰恰相反，正是生产率提升受到的限制，解释了为什么这些国家的教育发展没有更快。

articles.title: 阅读四 · 新英格兰早期移民的不同思想背景
articles.context: 殖民时期思想史。文章先介绍新英格兰牧师和政治精英的知识传统，再提醒读者普通移民的教育与信仰背景更为多样，借约翰·戴恩和沿海移民说明民间迷信、宗教与现实动机并存。语气历史叙述、克制分析。
rows: The most thoroughly studied intellectuals in the history of the New World are the ministers and political leaders of seventeenth-century New England.
在新大陆历史上，被研究得最为深入的知识分子，是17世纪新英格兰的牧师和政治领袖。
According to the standard history of American philosophy, nowhere else in colonial America was ‘so much importance attached to intellectual pursuits.’
按照美国哲学史的传统叙述，在殖民时期的美洲，没有其他地方像新英格兰这样“如此重视知识追求”。
According to many books and articles, New England's leaders established the basic themes and preoccupations of an unfolding, dominant Puritan tradition in American intellectual life.
许多书籍和文章认为，新英格兰领袖确立了美国思想生活中逐渐展开并占据主导地位的清教传统的基本主题与核心关切。
To take this approach to the New Englanders normally means to start with the Puritans' theological innovations and their distinctive ideas about the church—important subjects that we may not neglect.
按照这种方式研究新英格兰人，通常要从清教徒在神学上的创新以及他们对教会的独特看法谈起——这些当然都是不可忽视的重要主题。
But in keeping with our examination of southern intellectual life, we may consider the original Puritans as carriers of European culture, adjusting to New World circumstances.
但与我们考察南方思想生活的方式一致，我们也可以把最初的清教徒看作欧洲文化的携带者，他们正在适应新大陆的环境。
The New England colonies were the scenes of important episodes in the pursuit of widely understood ideals of civility and virtuosity.
新英格兰殖民地也见证了人们追求广泛认同的文明与才艺理想的重要历程。
The early settlers of Massachusetts Bay included men of impressive education and influence in England.
马萨诸塞湾早期移民中，有一些人在英国就受过良好教育并具有相当影响力。

Besides the ninety or so learned ministers who came to Massachusetts churches in the decade after 1629, there were political leaders like John Winthrop, an educated gentleman, lawyer, and official of the Crown before he journeyed to Boston.
除了1629年后十年间来到马萨诸塞各教会的大约90名博学牧师外，还有约翰·温斯罗普这样的政治领袖；他在前往波士顿之前，是受过教育的绅士、律师和王室官员。
These men wrote and published extensively, reaching both New World and Old World audiences, and giving New England an atmosphere of intellectual earnestness.
这些人大量写作并出版作品，读者遍及新旧大陆，也由此赋予新英格兰一种严肃求知的思想氛围。
We should not forget, however, that most New Englanders were less well educated.
然而，我们不应忘记，大多数新英格兰人受教育程度并没有那么高。
While few craftsmen or farmers, let alone dependents and servants, left literary compositions to be analyzed, it is obvious that their views were less fully intellectualized.
工匠和农民留下可供分析的文字作品本就不多，更不用说家属和仆人了；显然，他们的观念并没有被充分知识化。
Their thinking often had a traditional superstitious quality.
他们的思维往往带有传统迷信色彩。
A tailor named John Dane, who emigrated in the late 1630s, left an account of his reasons for leaving England that is filled with signs.
一名叫约翰·戴恩的裁缝在17世纪30年代末移民，他留下了自己离开英国原因的记录，其中充满了各种征兆式的解释。

Sexual confusion, economic frustrations, and religious hope—all came together in a decisive moment when he opened the Bible, told his father that the first line he saw would settle his fate, and read the magical words: ‘Come out from among them, touch no unclean thing, and I will be your God and you shall be my people.’
性方面的困惑、经济上的挫折和宗教希望，在一个决定性的时刻交织到了一起：他打开《圣经》，告诉父亲自己看到的第一句话将决定命运，随后读到那句带有神秘力量的话：“你们务要从他们中间出来，不要沾不洁净的物；我要作你们的神，你们要作我的子民。”
One wonders what Dane thought of the careful sermons explaining the Bible that he heard in Puritan churches.
这不禁让人想知道，戴恩对清教教堂里那些细致解释《圣经》的布道究竟作何感想。
Meanwhile, many settlers had slighter religious commitments than Dane's, as one clergyman learned in confronting folk along the coast who mocked that they had not come to the New World for religion.
与此同时，许多移民的宗教投入甚至还不如戴恩；一位牧师在面对沿海居民时就发现，有人嘲讽说他们来到新大陆并不是为了宗教。
not come to the New World for religion
‘Our main end was to catch fish.’

articles.title: 新题型 · 人类学文化理论从进化论到传播论与功能论
articles.context: 人类学思想史。按原题正确匹配 C-E-B-A-G 还原正文，只保留真正进入文章的五个插入段，排除 D、F 两个干扰项。语气学术、清晰，人物与理论之间的转折关系要突出。
rows: Coinciding with the groundbreaking theory of biological evolution proposed by British naturalist Charles Darwin in the 1860s, British social philosopher Herbert Spencer put forward his own theory of biological and cultural evolution.
19世纪60年代，英国博物学家查尔斯·达尔文提出了开创性的生物进化论；几乎与此同时，英国社会哲学家赫伯特·斯宾塞也提出了自己的生物与文化进化理论。
Spencer argued that all worldly phenomena, including human societies, changed over time, advancing toward perfection.
斯宾塞认为，世间一切现象——包括人类社会——都会随时间变化，并朝着更加完善的方向发展。

He argued that human evolution was characterized by a struggle he called the ‘survival of the fittest,’ in which weaker races and societies must eventually be replaced by stronger, more advanced races and societies.
他认为，人类进化具有一种他称为“适者生存”的斗争特征，在这一过程中，较弱的种族和社会最终必然会被更强大、更先进的种族和社会取代。
American social scientist Lewis Henry Morgan introduced another theory of cultural evolution in the late 1800s.
19世纪后期，美国社会科学家刘易斯·亨利·摩尔根提出了另一种文化进化理论。
Morgan helped found modern anthropology—the scientific study of human societies, customs and beliefs—thus becoming one of the earliest anthropologists.
摩尔根参与奠定了现代人类学——即对人类社会、习俗和信仰进行科学研究的学科——因此成为最早的人类学家之一。
In his work, he attempted to show how all aspects of culture changed together in the evolution of societies.
在研究中，他试图说明文化的各个方面如何随着社会进化而共同发生变化。

Thus, in his view, diverse aspects of culture, such as the structure of families, forms of marriage, categories of kinship, ownership of property, forms of government, technology, and systems of food production, all changed as societies evolved.
因此在他看来，家庭结构、婚姻形式、亲属关系类型、财产所有制、政府形式、技术以及食物生产体系等不同文化要素，都会随着社会进化而变化。
In the early 1900s in North America, German-born American anthropologist Franz Boas developed a new theory of culture known as historical particularism.
20世纪初，在北美，出生于德国的美国人类学家弗朗茨·博厄斯提出了一种新的文化理论，称为历史特殊论。
Historical particularism, which emphasized the uniqueness of all cultures, gave new direction to anthropology.
历史特殊论强调每一种文化的独特性，为人类学提供了新的研究方向。
In order to study particular cultures as completely as possible, he became skilled in linguistics, the study of languages, and in physical anthropology, the study of human biology and anatomy.
为了尽可能完整地研究具体文化，他熟练掌握了语言学——研究语言的学科——以及体质人类学——研究人类生物特征和解剖结构的学科。
Boas felt that the culture of any society must be understood as the result of a unique history and not as one of many cultures belonging to a broader evolutionary stage or type of culture.
博厄斯认为，任何社会的文化都必须被理解为一段独特历史的产物，而不能仅仅把它视作属于某个更广泛进化阶段或文化类型的众多文化之一。
not as one of many cultures
Other anthropologists believed that cultural innovations, such as inventions, had a single origin and passed from society to society.
另一些人类学家则认为，发明等文化创新具有单一来源，随后从一个社会传播到另一个社会。
This theory was known as diffusionism.
这种理论被称为传播论。
Historical particularism became a dominant approach to the study of culture in American anthropology, largely through the influence of many students of Boas.
在博厄斯众多学生的影响下，历史特殊论后来成为美国人类学研究文化的主导方法。
But a number of anthropologists in the early 1900s also rejected the particularist theory of culture in favor of diffusionism.
但20世纪初，也有一些人类学家拒绝文化特殊论，转而支持传播论。
Some attributed virtually every important cultural achievement to the inventions of a few, especially gifted peoples that, according to diffusionists, then spread to other cultures.
有些人几乎把所有重要文化成就都归因于少数特别有天赋的民族所作的发明；按照传播论者的说法，这些发明随后传播到了其他文化。

For example, British anthropologists Grafton Elliot Smith and W. J. Perry incorrectly suggested, on the basis of inadequate information, that farming, pottery making, and metallurgy all originated in ancient Egypt and diffused throughout the world.
例如，英国人类学家格拉夫顿·埃利奥特·史密斯和 W. J. 佩里基于不充分的信息，错误地提出农业、制陶和冶金都起源于古埃及，并从那里传播到世界各地。
In fact, all of these cultural developments occurred separately at different times in many parts of the world.
事实上，这些文化发展都曾在世界许多地区的不同时期独立出现。
Also in the early 1900s, French sociologist Emile Durkheim developed a theory of culture that would greatly influence anthropology.
同样在20世纪初，法国社会学家埃米尔·涂尔干提出了一种后来对人类学产生重大影响的文化理论。
Durkheim proposed that religious beliefs functioned to reinforce social solidarity.
涂尔干提出，宗教信仰具有强化社会团结的功能。
An interest in the relationship between the function of society and culture became a major theme in European, and especially British, anthropology.
对社会与文化功能之间关系的关注，后来成为欧洲人类学、尤其是英国人类学的重要主题。

articles.title: 翻译 · 社会制度的教育作用与正式教育的形成
articles.context: 教育哲学与社会制度。只保留46-50五个划线目标句，围绕社会制度的间接教育作用、对青少年的塑造以及正式学校教育的产生展开。语气理性、抽象、清晰。
rows: It may be said that the measure of the worth of any social institution is its effect in enlarging and improving experience, but this effect is not a part of its original motive.
可以说，衡量任何社会制度价值的尺度，在于它能否扩大并改善人的经验；但这种作用并不是该制度最初形成时的动机之一。
not a part of its original motive
Only gradually was the by-product of the institution noted, and only more gradually still was this effect considered as a directive factor in the conduct of the institution.
人们只是逐渐注意到这种制度所产生的副作用，而又过了更长时间，才把这种作用视为指导制度运行的一个因素。
While it is easy to ignore in our contact with them the effect of our acts upon their disposition, it is not so easy as in dealing with adults.
在同年轻人交往时，我们虽然也容易忽视自己的行为会对他们的性情产生什么影响，但要像对待成年人那样对此完全不加理会，却没有那么容易。
Since our chief business with them is to enable them to share in a common life we cannot help considering whether or not we are forming the powers which will secure this ability.
既然我们与年轻人相处时最主要的任务，是使他们能够参与共同生活，我们就不能不考虑：自己是否正在培养那些能够保证他们具备这种能力的素质。
We are thus led to distinguish, within the broad educational process which we have been so far considering, a more formal kind of education—that of direct tuition or schooling.
因此，在我们迄今所讨论的广义教育过程中，我们进一步区分出一种更正式的教育形式，也就是直接教学或学校教育。
